key_insight: Aligning selected training-side rounding locations with inference stabilizes BF16 LLM reinforcement learning without matching the entire execution stack.
engineering_relevance: Targeted precision handling can prevent training collapse while leaving the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.
method: Align rounding locations in RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm.
Retain selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs.
Evaluate full three-region alignment and RoPE-path alignment alone.
evidence_signal: Across four Qwen-family models, three-region alignment prevented the collapse seen with default BF16; RoPE-path alignment alone also sufficed in the studied runs.
watch_item: RoPE-only sufficiency is established only for the studied runs, and numerical discrepancies remain after alignment.
paper_title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
